provenance.algorithm: Originals: (1) envelope = canonical JCS bytes of a fixed 12-field SignatureEnvelope via to_bytes(); (2) sealed = real ChainAssembler receipt, subject-bound envelope, ES256 RFC-6979 signature over envelope.signing_input(), serde JSON; (3) hybrid = real hybrid_sign output (ES256 DER + ML-DSA-65 over the same message), serde JSON. Mutation families per surface: byte flips at every 16th offset with XOR masks 0x01/0x80/0xFF (hybrid: stride 256 — its ML-DSA-65 half is a ~3309-element ~14 KB array; stride 16 would duplicate ~14 MB into the static corpus); truncation at 10/20/.../90/95/99 percent; valid-prefix-then-garbage tails; type substitutions string<->int (plus null/array/object) for each field including all 12 nested envelope fields of the sealed surface; unicode injection (invalid UTF-8 0xFF, legal multibyte C3 A9, control U+0007, unicode-escaped ASCII, UTF-8 BOM) and whitespace injection (pretty-print, inter-token spaces, trailing whitespace); empty documents (empty string, {}, null, []); deeply-nested JSON at depth 200 above serde_json's 128 recursion limit, whole-document and via ignored extra keys; duplicate JSON keys in raw text (equal-value duplicates are lawful accept-equal on sealed/hybrid only — the envelope surface excludes every non-semantic identity by the never-accept-equal law); oversized integers at the 2^53 JCS boundary (2^53, 2^53+1, u64::MAX, raw 2^64 token, u32 and u8 overflow targets). Classification was OBSERVED at generation time on the exact bytes/JSON committed here, then pinned: envelope from_bytes Err => refuse, Ok && != original => accept-different, Ok && == original forbidden; sealed/hybrid serde Ok or typed Err (never panic), Ok reserialized == original => any, else accept-different.
provenance.generator: w4-lane7 differential wire-format corpus generator v1 (scratch /tmp/w4-lane7; deterministic: fixed seeds 0xB7/0x5E/0x2A, fixed constants, no wall-clock, no OS RNG — a re-run reproduces this corpus byte-identically)
